mainEntity.name: What does the DUTCH test actually measure?

acceptedAnswer.text: It measures your sex hormones (like estrogen, progesterone, and testosterone), how your body metabolizes them, and your daily cortisol pattern, from dried-urine samples collected across a day. That gives a fuller picture than a single blood draw, especially for cycle, sleep, and adrenal symptoms.

mainEntity.name: How is DUTCH different from a regular hormone blood test?

acceptedAnswer.text: Blood gives one snapshot of total levels. DUTCH adds the metabolites (how your body is breaking hormones down) and a full-day cortisol rhythm, which often explains symptoms that bloodwork calls “normal.”

mainEntity.name: Do I collect the DUTCH test at home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. After your consult you receive an at-home kit and collect dried-urine samples at set times over a day, then send it to the lab. Dr. Nina reviews the results with you afterward.

mainEntity.name: Is the DUTCH test worth it?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is worth it when your symptoms point to hormones and the results will change your plan. Run for the right reason and interpreted by a clinician, it can shortcut a lot of guessing; run randomly with no one reading it, it is just paper.

mainEntity.name: Can I order a DUTCH test without a doctor?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can buy kits online, but you are then left to interpret a complex report alone. Here it is ordered off your symptoms and read by a physician who turns it into an actual plan.

mainEntity.name: Can I just do the test without becoming a patient?

acceptedAnswer.text: Testing here is always part of physician-led care. You start with a $99 Symptom Consultation so it is ordered for the right reason and the results are actually used.

sections.label: Hero

headings.text: DUTCH hormone testing in Atlanta, read by a physician who turns it into a plan.

paragraphs: If a standard blood panel keeps coming back “normal” while your cycles, sleep, and mood say otherwise, the problem was never in your head. It is that a single morning blood draw misses most of the hormone story.

I am Dr. Nina Ross, ND PhD. The DUTCH test maps your hormones and their metabolites across a full day, and I read it as one move inside a plan that treats what it uncovers. That is how a stack of numbers becomes an actual answer.

sections.label: What it is

headings.text: A full day of your hormones and their metabolites, mapped end to end.

paragraphs: The DUTCH test uses dried-urine samples across a day to measure your sex hormones, how your body breaks them down, and your cortisol rhythm. That depth is real and genuinely useful, and it pays off when a clinician reads it against your symptoms and turns it into a plan.
It shows not just your levels but how your body is processing them, which blood often misses.
Sampling across the day reveals the adrenal pattern behind wired-but-tired and broken sleep.
Dr. Nina interprets it against your symptoms and history, so the results actually mean something.

sections.label: Who it's for

headings.text: The DUTCH test is right for some people. It is wrong for others.

eyebrowSpans: It is not for you if
paragraphs: If that second list stung a little, good. That honesty is exactly what you are paying for here.

boldPairs.body: Your symptoms scream hormones but standard bloodwork keeps reading “normal”
You are navigating perimenopause, menopause, PCOS, or stubborn cycle issues

boldPairs.title: It is not for you if

You expect one panel to replace an ongoing relationship with a clinician
